# Review round 3 — gateway/session_cache.py

## code-reviewer

`get_session` (session_cache.py:10) — Blocker.

The module-level `_CACHE` dict is mutated on every request. The gateway runs
its handlers on a thread pool, so two threads can hit the miss path for the
same `session_id` concurrently, both call `loader`, and both write. The
eviction branch is worse: `min()` walks the dict while another thread may be
inserting. This needs a lock or a thread-safe cache type before merge.

## codex

`get_session` (session_cache.py:10) — Nit, non-blocking.

CPython dict operations are atomic under the GIL, so the reads and writes here
cannot corrupt the dict. A duplicate `loader` call on a cold key is idempotent
and costs one extra fetch. Adding a lock on the hot path would serialize every
authenticated request for no correctness gain. Ship it; revisit only if the
cache ever moves off a single process.
